Honey and fruit juice concentrate are generally treated as added sugars, even though they come from natural sources. A "no added sugar" claim on the front can still sit beside them, so the ingredients list on the back is the better guide. Ingredients are listed from most to least by weight, so anything near the top is a larger part of the product. If you want to avoid sugar, look for honey, syrup, juice concentrate or anything ending in "-ose", and check the "added sugars" line on the nutrition table if there is one. I can't give medical or dietary advice, so for a health condition your doctor or dietitian is the best person to ask.

The line about a facility that handles nuts is a cross-contact warning. It means traces of nuts may be present even though nuts are not listed as an ingredient. If anyone eating this has a nut allergy, please don't rely on the front of the box. Read the allergen line each time, and check with your doctor on what is safe for you.
